title: RBACv2 audit simulation and SIEM ingest playbook
body:
Purpose:
This is a pragmatic pre-audit playbook used to rehearse auditor requests around RBACv2, our audit-log schema, SIEM export transforms, and evidence automation. It is scoped to SOC 2 / ISO 27001 control families that depend on access control, privileged access logging, and log retention/export (SOC2 CC6, ISO A.9/A.12/A.8.1).

Scope and intended use:
- Simulation of typical auditor asks (control crosswalks, sample evidence, query results)
- Checklist for on-call SRE/security engineer to run quick evidence pulls during auditor interviews
- Reference for engineers who implement SIEM mapping and log-export transforms

Quick summary (one-line):
We produce per-request, per-actor RBAC decision logs with a stable schema, a nightly SIEM export pipeline (ECS-compatible fields), and an evidence automation layer that snapshots policy versions and user-role history for attestations. Known gaps in current sprint are retention tuning and sampling for high-volume endpoints (see Gaps).

Control mapping narrative (how RBACv2 artifacts satisfy audit objectives):
- Access control design (ISO A.9 / SOC2 CC6): policy artifacts + role definitions + versioned policy bundle (policy_version field) show that authorization is centralized and versioned.
- Authentication and session traceability (ISO A.9.4 / SOC2): audit logs include actor_id, principal_email, request_id, correlation_id and session_id to tie actions back to identity.
- Change control for authorization policies (ISO A.12 / SOC2): policy change events (policy_change: {author, diff, change_id}) are captured and stored for rollback and reviewer trace.
- Monitoring and logging (ISO A.12.4 / SOC2): SIEM exports map decision outcomes and enforcement points with host, region, and request metadata to enable alerting and forensic reconstruction.

Evidence inventory (what we produce and where to pull it):
- Policy bundle snapshots (S3): path s3://redwood-compliance/policies/rbacv2/YYYY-MM-DD.policy.json (contains policy_version, commit_hash, author, changelog)
- Role assignment history (DB export): CSV extracts per-user with timestamps and actor that made the assignment (retention: 2 years snapshot)
- Authorization decision logs (primary source): GZIP'd JSON lines (newline-delimited) stored in archive-bucket with index (by request_id and actor_id) for 730 days by policy
- Policy change tickets and approvals: JIRA links (JIRA-SEC-412, JIRA-SEC-421) with reviewer comments
- SIEM exported indices: nightly indices in Elastic: rbac-decisions-YYYY.MM.DD and a summarized daily index rbac-decisions-summary-YYYY-MM-DD

Audit pull checklist (run during interview):
1) Identify control ask (e.g., "show successful privilege escalations in last 90 days").
2) Confirm date window and scope (user set, service account, region).
3) Pull policy snapshot for time T (S3 path) to show policy in effect.
4) Query authorization decision logs for request types and actor(s).
5) Correlate with role assignment history and ticket evidence.
6) Package results as CSV + sample log lines + pointer to policy bundle + pointer to SIEM dashboard; upload to auditor share link.

Sample authorization decision log (single line, newline-delimited JSON stored in archive):
{"timestamp":"2025-02-14T22:41:03Z","request_id":"req_9f8a3b","correlation_id":"corr_33e2","actor_id":"u_87d2","principal_email":"alice@customer.com","service":"model-serving","resource_type":"model.endpoint","resource_id":"m-endpoint-231","action":"invoke","decision":"deny","reason":"rate_limit_exceeded","policy_version":"v2025-02-10-3","policy_change_id":"chg_118","decision_latency_ms":12,"enforce_point":"edge-proxy","client_ip":"18.205.22.14"}

SIEM mapping notes (we export under ECS-compatible keys where possible):
- ecs.actor.id => actor_id
- ecs.actor.email => principal_email
- ecs.event.id => request_id
- ecs.event.action => action
- ecs.event.outcome => decision (success | failure | deny)
- ecs.event.duration => decision_latency_ms
- ecs.network.direction => outbound/inbound inferred from service
- custom.rbac.policy_version => policy_version
- custom.rbac.policy_change => policy_change_id

Sample Elastic query (KQL) to answer "show denies for privileged actions in last 30 days":
index=rbac-decisions-* AND event.action:("grant-role" OR "assign-role" OR "promote") AND event.outcome:deny AND @timestamp:[now-30d TO now] | sort @timestamp desc | limit 500

Sample Splunk SPL for same ask:
index=rbac_decisions earliest=-30d@d latest=now event.action=(grant-role OR assign-role OR promote) event.outcome=deny | table _time actor_id principal_email request_id action reason policy_version | sort -_time | head 500

Evidence packaging recommendations (what auditors expect):
- Include the exact policy bundle file for the request time and the file checksum.
- Provide 10 representative log lines (anonymize customer PII when required) plus a compressed archive of full matched lines.
- Provide a small runbook that shows how the logs were pulled (script + KQL/SPL query) so auditor can see reproducibility.

Known gaps and recommended mitigations (current sprint items):
1) High-volume endpoints occasionally drop DEBUG-level decision metadata in sampling mode — mitigation: temporary increase sampling for endpoints under audit plus backfill script (JIRA-SEC-433).
2) Retention policy for derived SIEM daily summaries is 90 days, while auditors sometimes ask for 1 year summaries — mitigation: extend summary retention to 13 months for compliance buckets.
3) No automated snapshot for role-assignment CSV for rolling 12-month attestations — mitigation: schedule monthly snapshot job and store versions in compliance S3 prefix.

Rapid troubleshooting cues (for SRE/security responder):
- If auditor requests a log that isn’t in the archive, search active hot-warm indices and check ingestion pipeline (Logstash/Fluentd) last 24h metrics.
- If request_id not found, check the frontend proxy for request-id rewrites; correlate by correlation_id or session_id.
- If SIEM field missing, check transform pipeline mapping (transformer service v2.1) for field drop rules.

Prepared auditor Q&A (short answers you can read aloud):
Q1: How do you tie an action back to an identity?
A1: Every authorization decision includes actor_id, principal_email and request_id. We map actor_id to identity provider (OIDC subject) and can show the authenticated session token issued at the time.

Q2: How are policy changes reviewed and approved?
A2: Policy changes are proposed via PR (GitHub) with mandatory peer review and an entry in the policy-change log that includes approver id and JIRA ticket; the approved bundle is snapshotted to the S3 compliance bucket.

Q3: Can you prove the policy in effect at the time of a denied request?
A3: Yes — we retrieve the policy bundle by policy_version from S3 and show the change_id referenced in the log line. The bundle includes a checksum and commit metadata.

Q4: How long do you retain raw decision logs?
A4: Raw auth decision logs are retained 730 days in cold archive; hot indices are kept 90 days for fast queries.

Q5: How do you ensure logs were not tampered with?
A5: Each daily archive manifests includes file checksums and is written to an immutable compliance S3 prefix with restricted ACLs and bucket-level object lock for a configurable retention period.

Q6: Do you export PII to third-party SIEM providers?
A6: No PII fields (principal_email) are hashed unless specifically approved in an export policy. Exports default to hashed_email and actor_id. Approval tickets exist for exceptions.

Q7: What happens during a model-serving failover — are decisions still logged?
A7: Yes — log writing is a local async buffer and agent persists to local WAL; on failover agents replay to central collector. Replay idempotency is enforced by request_id.

Q8: Can you reproduce a stateful denial like a rate-limit block?
A8: Yes — rate-limiter emits decision events with reason and token_bucket state; we store the last known token_bucket snapshot in derived telemetry for the request window.

Q9: How do you handle service/service-account actions?
A9: Service accounts have dedicated actor namespaces (svc_) and we require MFA-bound approvals for grant-role actions. All service-to-service grants record the initiating human reviewer ticket id.

Q10: How do you validate your SIEM mappings?
A10: We run nightly validation jobs that replay a sampled set of decision logs through the export transform, then compare exported fields to expected ECS keys and flag schema drift.

Appendix: quick commands and links
- Pull last 500 denies for user u_87d2 (Elastic):
  curl -u readonly:token 'https://elastic.redwood/_search' -d '{"query":{"bool":{"must":[{"term":{"actor_id":"u_87d2"}},{"term":{"event.outcome":"deny"}}]},"size":500,"sort":[{"@timestamp":{"order":"desc"}}]}}'

- Playbook owner: Evelyn Chen (security-and-compliance)
- Next steps: schedule a dry-run with external auditor team, produce 30-day extended retention for summary indices, and land the monthly assignment snapshot job (JIRA-SEC-433).

Notes to reviewers: This is intentionally operational — please call out any missing artifacts that auditors have recently asked for (we had a Nov-2024 ask for longer summary retention).
